resources.string: Not running: notification access is off.
Running. NotiRegX checks this regularly and reconnects it if Android stops it.
Not running. Android disconnected it; tap Restart.
When off, every notification is let through but still shows up in Recent.
Older notifications are dropped from a rule\'s history beyond this.

Android buzzes before NotiRegX can remove a notification. Rules with De-buzz turned on silence their app instead, and NotiRegX buzzes itself for whatever gets through. A de-buzz rule for one app silences it right away; one for any app silences a notification category the first time it catches something from it. Turning De-buzz off or deleting the rule puts everything back.
This phone doesn\'t support companion devices, so De-buzz isn\'t available.
Android only allows this for apps linked to a companion device. Turn on Bluetooth and pick any nearby device (earbuds, watch, speaker, TV). Nothing is ever sent to it.
Before uninstalling NotiRegX, turn De-buzz off on every rule so the apps get their sound back.
Save your rules to a file, or add rules from one (yours or a friend\'s). History isn\'t included.
Required to read and filter notifications.
Optional. Lets \"Always alert\" rules ring through Do Not Disturb.
Stops the system from putting NotiRegX to sleep.

If Android says notification access is a \"restricted setting\", open App info, tap ⋮ in the corner and choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.\n\nTo keep filtering reliable, also add NotiRegX to Settings › Battery › Background usage limits › Never sleeping apps.
A range that ends before it starts runs overnight. Same start and end means all day.
The first %1$d within %2$d min get through; the rest are caught.
The bundle shows up as soon as something is caught.
The bundle stays hidden and shows up at these times.
Counts every notification, whatever your rules did with it. For chat apps the sender is the person or group; for others it\'s the notification\'s title. Tap one to make a rule.
